New York Transfer Tax: State, NYC and Local Rates, and Who Pays

Cash Home Buyers in New York
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling a New York House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is. Tell us about the property and the timeline.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from New York statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

New York charges a state real estate transfer tax of $2 for each $500 of consideration, and the seller pays it. Some places add their own taxes. This guide lists only what we confirmed on official pages.

What the official sources say

  • NY state real estate transfer tax: $2 for each $500 or fractional part of consideration on each conveyance of real property when consideration exceeds $500 (i.e., $2 per $500 = 0.4%). For 1-3 family houses and individual residential condo units, and conveyances under $500,000, consideration excludes the value of any lien/encumbrance remaining at conveyance. (NY Tax Law §1402(a); source)
  • Additional $1.25 per $500 of consideration applies to conveyances within a city of 1,000,000+ population when residential consideration is $3,000,000 or more (or $2,000,000+ for other property). 'Residential real property' includes a 1-3 family house, an individual condo unit, or a cooperative apartment unit. (NY Tax Law §1402(a)(2); source)
  • Additional ('mansion') tax: 1% of consideration on conveyance of residential real property (1-3 family house, individual condo unit, co-op unit) when consideration for the entire conveyance is $1,000,000 or more. Paid by the grantee; if grantee fails to pay or is exempt, the grantor has the duty to pay and liability is joint and several. (NY Tax Law §1402-a(a)-(b); source)
  • NYS Tax Dept: base transfer tax $2 per $500 of consideration (consideration > $500); additional 'mansion' tax 1% for residences at $1M+. For NYC conveyances from July 1, 2019: extra $1.25 per $500 for residential >= $3M (or other property >= $2M), plus a supplemental tax on residential >= $2M at incremental rates between 0.25% and 2.9% (rates in Form TP-584-NYC-I). (NYS DTF 'Real estate transfer tax' page (reviewed June 1, 2026); source)
  • Who pays: base tax and additional base tax are paid by the grantor (seller) (buyer pays if seller doesn't or is exempt); mansion tax and NYC supplemental tax are paid by the buyer (seller pays if buyer fails/is exempt, joint and several). (NYS DTF 'Real estate transfer tax' - Who pays the tax; source)
  • Filing: outside NYC, file Form TP-584 with the county clerk where the property is located; form and tax due no later than the 15th day after delivery of the deed. NYC conveyances use Form TP-584-NYC. If deed is not recorded, file with the Tax Department directly by the 15th day. (NYS DTF 'Real estate transfer tax' - File and pay tax; source)
  • Nontaxable conveyances include: conveyances without consideration/bona fide gifts, to secure a debt, tax-sale conveyances, partition deeds, Bankruptcy Act conveyances, mere change of identity with no change in beneficial ownership. 'Conveyance' includes mortgage foreclosure and transfer in lieu of foreclosure but excludes conveyance pursuant to devise, bequest or inheritance. (NYS DTF 'Real estate transfer tax' - Exemptions and Definitions; source)
  • LLC rule: when an LLC is seller or buyer of a building with up to four dwelling units, TP-584 cannot be accepted without documentation identifying names and addresses of all members, managers and authorized persons (down to natural persons). (NYS DTF 'Real estate transfer tax' - Conveyances to or from an LLC; source)
  • NYC RPTT (city tax, Admin Code Title 11 Ch. 21; enabling Tax Law 1201(b)): residential 1-3 family house/condo/co-op: 1% if value $500,000 or less, 1.425% if more than $500,000; all other transfers: 1.425% if $500,000 or less, 2.625% if more. Applies when sale/transfer is more than $25,000. Return and payment due within 30 days after transfer; filed through ACRIS (NYC-RPT). Executor's deed per will terms is exempt but reportable; executor deed in connection with a sale is taxable. (NYC Dept of Finance, Real Property Transfer Tax (RPTT) page; source)
  • Mount Vernon: state enabling statute authorizes the city to impose a deed transfer tax at a rate not to exceed 1.5% of consideration, may allow lien deductions and an exemption up to $100,000; payment/return may be required as a condition precedent to recording. Actual adopted local rate/exemption not confirmed. (NY Tax Law §1205(b) (rev. 2025-12-12); source)
  • Peekskill: state enabling statute authorizes the city to impose a deed transfer tax at a rate not to exceed 1% of consideration, with optional lien deductions and exemption up to $100,000; contracts before Sept 1, 2007 not covered. Actual adopted local rate not confirmed. (NY Tax Law §1206(b); source)
Selling in New York?
We buy New York houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Filing and recording

  • Form TP-584 (Combined Real Estate Transfer Tax Return, Credit Line Mortgage Certificate, and Certification of Exemption from Payment of Estimated Personal Income Tax) is filed with the county clerk for property outside NYC (TP-584-NYC inside NYC) by the 15th day after delivery of the deed. (NYS DTF real estate transfer tax page; source)
  • Form RP-5217 (Real Property Transfer Report) filing fee is generally $125 for residential (1-3 family, rural residence, residential condo) and farm properties and $250 for all other properties; collected by the county clerk. (NYS DTF 'Filing Fees for Form RP-5217' (updated May 18, 2023); source)

What we could not confirm

  • The actual local transfer tax rates in Mount Vernon and Peekskill. State law only sets the maximum.

How to sell a New York house when this applies to you

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or court paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in New York.

New York transfer tax FAQ

Who pays the New York transfer tax?

The seller pays the base state tax. The buyer pays the mansion tax and the NYC supplemental tax, as described on the Department of Taxation and Finance page.

How do I file the transfer tax return?

Outside New York City, file Form TP-584 with the county clerk where the property sits. It is due no later than the 15th day after the deed is delivered.

Is an inherited house taxed on transfer?

State law excludes conveyances by devise, bequest or inheritance. NYC treats an executor deed given in connection with a sale as taxable.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.

Update registration after ownership change (marriage, divorce, survivorship, trust, etc.); close registration if you sell the property. (NYS DTF 'Register for STAR' (updated July 14, 2026); source)

New York Property Tax Guide: Grievance Day, STAR, Tax Liens and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in New York
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from New York statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

New York property tax is set and collected locally, so due dates and assessors differ by town, city and county. This guide covers the statewide rules we confirmed and points to local guides.

Grievance and appeals

  • Grievance: file Form RP-524 (outside NYC and Nassau) with the assessor or board of assessment review; deadline is Grievance Day, in most communities the fourth Tuesday in May. Exceptions: Suffolk third Tuesday in May; Westchester towns third Tuesday in June; assessing villages typically third Tuesday of February; NYC complaints by March 15 (Class One) / March 1 (others); Nassau March 1. Only the current tentative roll can be grieved; no cost and no lawyer required. (NYS DTF 'Grievance procedures' (updated May 8, 2026); source)
  • If BAR relief is denied: Small Claims Assessment Review (SCAR) for owner-occupied 1-3 family homes (or small vacant land), $30 fee; or tax certiorari in State Supreme Court under Article 7 of the Real Property Tax Law. Both must start within 30 days of filing of the final assessment roll or notice of filing, whichever is later. (NYS DTF 'Grievance procedures'; RPTL Art. 7; source)

STAR

  • STAR: Basic STAR is for owner-occupied primary residences; income limit $500,000 for the Basic STAR credit ($250,000 for the Basic STAR exemption); based on the first $30,000 of full value. Enhanced STAR is for primary residences of seniors age 65+ with qualifying income of $110,750 or less for the 2026-27 school year and $113,550 or less for 2027-28; based on first $91,700 of full value for 2027-28. STAR applies only to school district taxes (except partly to city taxes in NYC, Buffalo, Rochester, Yonkers, Syracuse). (NYS DTF 'Types of STAR' (updated Oct 27, 2026); source)
  • STAR registration: register once via the Homeowner Benefit Portal in Individual Online Services; DTF issues the STAR credit payment each year if eligible. New homeowners should register as soon as the home becomes their primary residence. Update registration after ownership change (marriage, divorce, survivorship, trust, etc.); close registration if you sell the property. (NYS DTF 'Register for STAR' (updated July 14, 2026); source)
Behind on property tax?
We buy New York houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

Tax liens and unpaid tax

  • RPTL 1110: real property subject to a delinquent tax lien may be redeemed by paying the enforcing officer the lien amount plus lawful charges on or before the end of the redemption period; the redemption period expires two years after lien date, though tax districts may lengthen it for residential/farm property (RPTL 1111) or shorten it to one year for vacant and abandoned residential property (1111-a), and a published notice (1124) may specify a later date. (NY RPTL §1110(1)-(2) (rev. 2019-12-27); source)
  • NYC tax lien sale: City sells unpaid property tax/water-sewer/other charge liens to a single authorized buyer (not the public); it is not a sale of the property but can lead to foreclosure. Lienholder may charge a 5% surcharge plus interest compounded daily at 6% (assessed value <= $250,000), 9% ($250,000-$450,000) or 16% (> $450,000), plus ~$300 admin costs. Foreclosure may begin within one year after the sale if unpaid. Eligibility e.g. 1-family owner-occupied: $5,000 property tax debt (3 years). 2025 sale held June 3, 2025. 5% surcharge waiver for primary-residence owners with combined income no greater than $110,750. (NYC Dept of Finance, Lien sales page; source)
  • Transfers given in connection with a tax sale are nontaxable conveyances for state transfer tax purposes. (NYS DTF real estate transfer tax page; source)

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or court paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in New York.

What a cash sale of a New York house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in New York.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required New York disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in New York

  • Ask the title company what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in New York change, so confirm details with the official office or a New York attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in New York

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

New York property tax FAQ

When is Grievance Day in New York?

In most communities it is the fourth Tuesday in May. Suffolk and Westchester use different days, and NYC uses its own Tax Commission dates.

What is the redemption period on a New York tax lien?

RPTL 1110 sets a two-year redemption period for a delinquent tax lien, starting from the lien date.
